description.narrative: UN June 2024 report estimates that 707,000 people have moved to South Sudan through various border points - 80% are South Sudanese returnees and 20% refugees. South Sudan struggles to provide basic services such as food, water, sanitation, healthcare, and protection to these vulnerable people. UNHCR estimates the displaced population staying in transit camps in Renk County is 22% children, 49% men and boys, 51% women and girls, and 15% people with disabilities. Refugees and returnees are expected to stay in transit camps for one week and then move to more permanent locations. According to UNHCR, 40,000 newly displaced arrivals are expected in July 2024. Services in the transit Centre and surrounding host communities are poor and identified gaps include WASH (latrines, SWM, NFIs); food, emergency shelter/housing, protection and GBV support. CTP, through its partner ADA, is already implementing an emergency project with funding from Irish Aid. It includes water trucking, WASH and FSL programming in Renk Transit Centre (TC). Given the increasing numbers of returnees and refugees from Sudan and the escalating needs, the support of internal Sudan Appeal funding is requested to allow CTP to strengthen the response to this new acute crisis through WASH and FSL programming over an extended period. Activities include: - Mass media and door to door visits to improve awareness of key personal hygiene behaviors to benefit 9000 returnees and host communities to improve sanitation and hygiene. - Distribution of 200 hygiene kits for girls and women. - Distribution of seeds and tools to benefit 300 returnees and host community households. - 9000 refugee, returnees and host community household benefit from improved sanitation and hygiene. - 300 returnees and host community household to benefit from enhanced food security in the midterm.
